mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 1.5% for two consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 1.5% and remains above for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with FEDFUNDS change (p > 0.05) in the identified regime.

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment momentum as measured by monthly PAYEMS exceeds 200,000 jobs, indicating labor market strength that supports corporate earnings growth and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: Payroll growth does not correlate with SPX 20-day forward returns (Pearson's rho < 0.2) in the observed period.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (GDPC1) by more than 10% in a month signals weakening aggregate demand, which predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls by more than 10% in a single month
failure_condition: GDPC1 declines >10% but SPX 5-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the Industrial Production index (INDPRO) below 100 for three consecutive months suggests supply-side softness that reduces investor confidence and yields negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO remains below 100 for three consecutive months
failure_condition: No significant negative relationship between INDPRO and SPX 20-day forward returns (Granger causality fails).

mechanism_narrative: When the Unemployment Rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.5% for two consecutive months, it indicates labor market resilience that lowers policy rate expectations and supports equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses below 4.5% and remains below for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no positive deviation from a baseline model (AICc not improved).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising Consumer Employment (HOUST) above 10,000 units signal labor market expansion that coincides with corporate hiring and positive investor sentiment, driving S&P 500 forward returns upward over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by more than 10,000 units in a month and remains elevated for the next month
failure_condition: No significant positive return predictability (t-test p > 0.05) when HOUST is the leading indicator.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in both industrial production (GDPC1) and consumer confidence (HOUST) over the same month create a dual-demand shock that increases perceived economic vulnerability and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < prev and HOUST < prev in the same month
failure_condition: Interaction term (GDPC1 * HOUST) is not statistically significant in explaining SPX 5-day returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rising above 4%), the negative impact on discount rates outweighs the positive effect of low inflation (CPIAUCSL < 250), producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% and remains above for two months
failure_condition: In tightening regimes, SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from a constant model (F-test p > 0.05).
